faqs.question: What is P4PRO with AffiPump used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact SPR system that runs both static screening and full flow-based kinetic characterization, kon, koff, and KD, on the same instrument.

faqs.question: How is P4PRO different from the P4SPR 2.0?
faqs.answer: P4PRO paired with the AffiPump adds flow mode and full kinetic measurement on top of the static screening capability the P4SPR 2.0 offers, without needing separate hardware.

faqs.question: Do I need to reconfigure the instrument to switch between static and flow mode?
faqs.answer: No, P4PRO switches between static and flow operation without reconfiguring the setup.

faqs.question: What kinetic parameters can P4PRO measure?
faqs.answer: Association rate (kon) from 10³ to 10⁷ M⁻¹s⁻¹, dissociation rate (koff) from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹, and KD calculated from both.

faqs.question: How much sample does a flow-mode run require?
faqs.answer: Between 5 and 100 µL per injection in flow mode, or 300 µL for static mode runs.

faqs.question: What sensor chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: Covalent surfaces like carboxyl, CMD, and AffiCoat for EDC/NHS coupling, plus capture-based surfaces including Anti-His, NTA, Protein A/G, Streptavidin, Strep-Tactin XT, and Anti-AAVX.

faqs.question: Do sensors need cleaning between runs?
faqs.answer: No, sensors are disposable and pre-characterized, eliminating cleaning and carry-over entirely.

faqs.question: What software does P4PRO run on?
faqs.answer: Affilabs.core, which includes Sparq, a built-in operation support assistant, and is shared across the P4 instrument platform.

faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the sensor chemistry and flow configuration needed.

longForm.heroHook: Static screening and full flow kinetics. One instrument, no reconfiguring.
longForm.heroLead: Most labs end up choosing between fast static screening and precise flow-based kinetics, then buying two instruments to get both. P4PRO paired with the AffiPump does both on one bench, switching between static and flow mode without swapping hardware or rebuilding the setup. Flow mode delivers full kinetic characterization, kon, koff, and KD, across a detection limit down to fM, while the same platform runs quick static screening when speed matters more than depth. Four simultaneous channels, semi-automated injection, and sample volumes as low as 5 µL in flow mode keep every run lean.

stats.label: No reconfiguration needed to switch modes

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: P4PRO and AffiPump product information: hybrid static/flow operation, kinetic range, and sensor compatibility.
body: P4PRO with AffiPump runs both static and flow-based SPR experiments on one instrument, switching modes without reconfiguring the setup.
Detection limit reaches fM, assay dependent, with KD measurable down to pM and beyond.
Flow mode unlocks full kinetic characterization: kon from 10³ to 10⁷ M⁻¹s⁻¹, koff from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹, and KD calculated directly from both.
Four simultaneous channels run sample and controls together in one injection, whether in static or flow mode.
Flow injection uses just 5 to 100 µL of sample, and static mode uses 300 µL, keeping precious sample material to a minimum either way.
Semi-automated injection cuts hands-on time per run, and direct inline controls give real-time feedback during every measurement.
Disposable, pre-characterized gold sensor chips eliminate cleaning and carry-over between runs, available in covalent and capture-based chemistries.
The same sensors and Affilabs.core software run across both P4PRO and the simpler P4SPR 2.0, so a lab can standardize on one software platform regardless of which instrument handles a given assay.

sections.title: Full Kinetic Characterization
sections.description: A binding signal alone tells you two molecules interact. kon, koff, and KD tell you how fast, how tightly, and whether that interaction holds up under real conditions, information static screening alone can't provide.
body: Flow mode measures association rate (kon) from 10³ to 10⁷ M⁻¹s⁻¹ and dissociation rate (koff) from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹, covering everything from fast, weak interactions to slow, tight ones.
Real acquisition data from a Protein A and IgG interaction shows full association and dissociation curves with a global fit, the kind of dataset drug discovery and QC teams need to defend a result.
Four channels keep that kinetic work efficient, running test conditions and controls together rather than in separate sequential runs.

faqs.question: What is P4SPR 2.0 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact, static SPR biosensor for real-time, label-free binding data, built for method development, teaching, and screening without flow-based complexity.

faqs.question: How is P4SPR 2.0 different from P4PRO?
faqs.answer: P4SPR 2.0 runs static mode only, while P4PRO adds flow mode via the AffiPump for full kon/koff kinetic measurement on the same platform.

faqs.question: Does P4SPR 2.0 need a pump or fluidics?
faqs.answer: No, it runs entirely static, with no pump, no fluidics, and no clogging risk.

faqs.question: How long does one run cycle take?
faqs.answer: 10 minutes or less, supporting fast iterative assay development and condition screening.

faqs.question: How much sample does each injection require?
faqs.answer: 150 µL per injection.

faqs.question: Can P4SPR 2.0 run without a dedicated power supply?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's laptop powered and works wherever the laptop does, no separate power setup required.

faqs.question: What sensor chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: Covalent surfaces like carboxyl, CMD, and AffiCoat for EDC/NHS coupling, plus capture-based surfaces including Anti-His, NTA, Protein A/G, Streptavidin, Strep-Tactin XT, and Anti-AAVX.

faqs.question: Do sensors need cleaning between runs?
faqs.answer: No, sensors are disposable and pre-characterized, eliminating cleaning and carry-over entirely.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade to flow-based kinetics later?
faqs.answer: Yes, P4SPR 2.0 shares sensors and Affilabs.core software with the flow-capable P4PRO, easing any future move to kinetic characterization.
